catalogue_requests.reason: cap.motion.joint_position.v1 takes a flat joint_positions array and requires reached and joint_positions outputs. The pinned controller action is control_msgs/action/FollowJointTrajectory: its goal is trajectory.points, an array of point objects carrying positions and time_from_start, and its terminal result is error_code and error_string. RosDriver argument targets cannot address array indices, so the flat class cannot be placed into trajectory.points; the class output also does not match the native terminal result. The extension preserves the controller's trajectory goal and terminal semantics.
catalogue_requests.summary: Send FollowJointTrajectory points through /joint_trajectory_controller/follow_joint_trajectory and report the controller's terminal error_code.

catalogue_requests.reason: cap.sensing.read.v1 is restricted to the sensor, sensor.imu and sensor.force_torque resource kinds. This device is robot.arm, and the pinned observation is a sensor_msgs/msg/JointState message with parallel name, position and velocity arrays. The extension carries that native message shape without relabelling the arm as a sensor.

No catalogue class re-activates a ros2_control controller through controller_manager's switch_controller; it is the declared re-enable (CORE-086) after the e-stop's deactivation, an input-free extension command whose output reports only that the switch answered ok.

notes:
BLOCKED: the primary arm trajectory action and the /joint_states observation are implemented and fake-tested, but the pinned clone exposes no source-backed stop, pause, controller-switch or safe-state action. The only motion endpoint is the acknowledged FollowJointTrajectory action at /joint_trajectory_controller/follow_joint_trajectory (bcr_arm_gazebo/scripts/control_arm_cli.py:18-22); the only observation used here is /joint_states (bcr_arm_gazebo/launch/bringup.gazebo.launch.py:209). The Gazebo world-control service and the controller_manager switch service are outside the clone and are not bridged by the upstream launch, so the package cannot cite a stop endpoint. The runtime software latch refuses new commands but cannot interrupt a trajectory the external joint_trajectory_controller has already accepted; the package therefore declares no safe_state.achieved_by, no estop_physical_ref and no safe-state action, and it does not claim a stopped state.

The final gate run fails G6 and G8 and skips G9 after G8: G6.ESTOP_FAILED reports status failed with MHS.SAFETY.SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED; G8 SAFE-028 reports e-stop receipt failed and safe_state_achieved=false. G1-G5 and G7 pass. The digest is from this final run; the report is check-report.json. The package test suite passes because it asserts this specific safety refusal; the gate itself skips G9 because G8 failed. There are no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings, and the earlier G1.BYTECODE warning was cleared by removing the generated __pycache__.

Coverage: the acknowledged arm action carries the seven joint names in joint1..joint7 order and trajectory.points; the action input uses the same seven-position point shape and the controller's terminal error_code/error_string application predicate. Joint travel bounds are sourced from the mechanical xacro (joint1/3/5/7 -6.28..6.28 rad; joint2/4/6 -2.0..2.0 rad). The clone states no trajectory duration or nanosecond bound, so time_from_start.sec and nanosec are operator_required; site-limits.example.json supplies example-only values for the fake conformance run. The fake is a ROS-free recording transport at F0: all joint values, action results and error strings are placeholders, and it runs no Gazebo, gz_ros2_control, MoveIt, ROS graph or physics. The real /joint_states publisher, controller timing, interpolation, collisions, gravity and camera, /clock, /tf and MoveIt planning surfaces are not covered; the fire-and-forget /joint_trajectory_controller/joint_trajectory publication in test_arm_movement.py:13-15 is intentionally not exposed as a completed command.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: none in helper or family; the card's RosDriver is used for the ROS 2 topic/action interface. The package uses x-cap extensions because no catalogue class [...]

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Confirmed the author's block: the clone drives the arm only through the joint_trajectory_controller's FollowJointTrajectory action (control_arm_cli.py:18-22, 87-99) and names no stop, pause, controller-switch or Gazebo world-control endpoint (the controller manager and goal cancellation live in ros2_control, outside the clone), so with no e-stop binding the gate fails G6.ESTOP_FAILED and G8 SAFE-028 with the latch held, the honest outcome for a simulator (HELPER_MISSING). The action and /joint_states bindings, the sourced joint travel limits (bcr_arm_mech.urdf.xacro lines 146 to 356: -6.28..6.28 rad for joints 1, 3, 5 and 7, -2.0..2.0 rad for 2, 4 and 6), the operator_required Duration fields and all 16 facts were checked; the clone has no hardware interface, only gz_ros2_control, mock_components and an Isaac Sim topic system. For the next author: the binding's timeout_ms of 2000 narrows the action's execution (sdk/docs/ros-driver.md:145-147) while the Action allows 120 s and the example overlay 10 s trajectories, so any trajectory longer than 2 s would end as an unknown outcome; and the fact citing control_arm_cli.py:21 for the ActionClient construction should cite 18-22. Risk R2 is above what a simulated arm needs but is allowed and was kept. The reviewer changed no authored file; the gate re-run rewrote check-report.json with the same findings. For the human reviewer: Simulation only. The JointTrajectoryController keeps executing an accepted trajectory after the MHS latch; nothing in the clone pauses Gazebo or switches the controller. Unblocking needs an acknowledged stop the clone names, or an SDK profile for a ros2_control controller switch or Gazebo world-control service.
